I have been farming these 6.5 mu for fifty years, and the wheat-maize rotation is what works on our plain. I am alone in the household now, so I cannot do heavy labor myself — I hire the combine and the rotary tiller from the village service team. That cost I plan for every season.

For winter wheat, I plant in early October after the maize comes off. I use improved semi-dwarf varieties — Jimai or Shi varieties, whatever the seed dealer has fresh. I broadcast about 15 kg of seed per mu because I sow a bit heavy; at my age I would rather have thick stand than worry about gaps. Base fertilizer I apply as compound 15-15-15, about 50 kg per mu before rotary tillage, then top-dress urea at jointing in March — around 20 kg of urea per mu. That gives me roughly 22-23 kg of pure nitrogen, which is what wheat on this soil needs. Our soil here is calcareous loam, phosphorus locks up, so I do not skimp on P. Potassium I keep moderate since the stubble return gives some back.

Wheat irrigation: I water the winter freeze-in around late November, then returning-green in early March, then jointing, then grain-filling. Four times total from the well. Herbicide once in spring for ryegrass, and one aphid spray at heading. Sometimes I add a flag-leaf spray if rust shows up — call it two pesticide rounds, three if the year is bad.

For summer maize after wheat, I use no-till direct seeding with a hybrid — Zhengdan or Denghai series. About 4500 plants per mu, so 2.5 kg of seed. Maize is hungrier than wheat for nitrogen. I put a starter compound at sowing, maybe 30 kg per mu, then side-dress urea at big-trumpet stage, around 25 kg urea per mu. Total N comes to about 24 kg per mu — neighbors who push 30 kg do not get much more yield, just waste. Phosphorus lower than wheat because residual carries over. Irrigation one or two times — July-August usually has enough rain, but if a dry spell hits at tasseling I must water or the ears will be short. Pesticide: one for armyworm or borer, one for aphids/mites late. Two rounds normally.

My yield target is what I have averaged: wheat around 480 kg/mu, maize around 560 kg/mu. I do not chase the highest numbers — the cost of the extra fertilizer and water eats the gain. But I will not cut inputs and gamble on a bad harvest either. At my age, a failed crop is not something I can recover from easily.
